target: Se eu soubesse cozinhar como ela, abriria um restaurante.
english: If I could cook like her, I'd open a restaurant.
tip: For know-how, 'could cook' uses saber, not poder: se eu soubesse cozinhar is 'if I could cook'.

target: Quem estuda passa.
english: Those who study pass.
tip: Here quem means whoever or those who, and it takes a singular verb, so estuda and passa.

target: Tudo que ele disse é verdade.
english: Everything he said is true.
tip: Tudo que is a set relative phrase for everything that; Brazilians usually drop the o of tudo o que.

target: Eu tenho corrido todas as manhãs.
english: I've been running every morning.
tip: Ter plus a participle, tenho corrido, means an action repeated up to now, not one finished event like English present perfect.

target: Come-se bem neste restaurante.
english: One eats well at this restaurant.
tip: come-se bem means 'one eats well'; the se leaves the verb with no named subject, like English 'one' or 'you'.

target: Gosto de pessoas que são sinceras.
english: I like people who are sincere.
tip: Gostar always needs de before its object, so it is gosto de pessoas, never gosto pessoas.

target: A forma como ele fala é engraçada.
english: The way he talks is funny.
tip: 'Como' can function as a relative pronoun meaning 'the way in which'.

target: A série que estou assistindo é viciante.
english: The series I'm watching is addictive.
tip: Assistir meaning to watch formally takes a before its object, but Brazilians drop it, as in a série que estou assistindo.

target: A gente tem se comunicado por videochamada.
english: We've been communicating by video call.
tip: A gente means we but takes a singular verb, so it is a gente tem se comunicado, never têm.

target: O dia em que nos conhecemos foi especial.
english: The day we met was special.
tip: For a point in time a relative clause uses em que, not quando, so o dia em que nos conhecemos.

target: Ele falou como se soubesse tudo.
english: He spoke as if he knew everything.
tip: Como se, meaning as if, takes the imperfect subjunctive, giving soubesse rather than the indicative sabia.

target: Se eu tivesse paciência, ensinaria crianças.
english: If I had patience, I would teach children.
tip: For a hypothetical, se plus the imperfect subjunctive tivesse pairs with the conditional ensinaria.

target: A escola onde estudei fica no centro.
english: The school where I studied is downtown.
tip: For where a place is located, ficar is the natural verb, so a escola fica no centro means it sits downtown.

target: A empresa onde ele estagiou o contratou.
english: The company where he interned hired him.
tip: The object pronoun o here means him and sits before the verb, o contratou, meaning hired him.

target: Ela tinha coberto o bolo com chocolate.
english: She had covered the cake with chocolate.
tip: Cobrir has the irregular participle coberto, not cobrido, as in tinha coberto o bolo.

target: Quem dera eu pudesse tirar férias agora.
english: If only I could take vacation now.
tip: Quem dera expresses a wish, if only, and is followed by the imperfect subjunctive pudesse.

target: O projeto no qual estamos trabalhando é complexo.
english: The project we're working on is complex.
tip: After a preposition, Portuguese often uses o qual, so trabalhar em gives o projeto no qual estamos trabalhando.

target: Nós tínhamos pagado a conta antes de sair.
english: We had paid the bill before leaving.
tip: Pagar has two participles; with ter use pagado, as in tínhamos pagado, while pago goes with ser or estar.

target: Eu tenho procurado emprego desde janeiro.
english: I've been looking for a job since January.
tip: Procurar means look for and takes a direct object, so procurado emprego, with no preposition after it.

target: Era importante que todos soubessem a notícia.
english: It was important that everyone knew the news.
tip: An impersonal opinion like era importante que forces the subjunctive, so soubessem, not sabiam.

target: Ele tinha descoberto a verdade antes de todo mundo.
english: He had discovered the truth before everyone else.
tip: Todo mundo means everyone but takes a singular verb, as in todo mundo sabe, never todo mundo sabem.

target: Quem não tem cão, caça com gato.
english: Whoever doesn't have a dog, hunts with a cat.
tip: caça com gato, 'hunts with a cat', is a saying: you make do with what you have.

target: Vende-se apartamento de dois quartos.
english: Two-bedroom apartment for sale.
tip: Adding -se to a verb forms an impersonal passive: vende-se apartamento = apartment for sale, no seller named.

target: Ele tem praticado esportes regularmente.
english: He's been practicing sports regularly.
tip: The present perfect with tem, as in tem praticado, means an ongoing or repeated action up to now, not one finished event.

target: Ele tinha se formado em engenharia.
english: He had graduated in engineering.
tip: formar-se means to graduate; in compound tenses the se sits between tinha and formado: tinha se formado.

target: Ele saiu sem que ninguém percebesse.
english: He left without anyone noticing.
tip: sem que (without) always triggers the subjunctive: sem que ninguém percebesse, never percebeu.

target: Vocês tinham visto esse filme antes?
english: Had you seen this movie before?
tip: ver has the irregular participle visto, not vido: tinham visto esse filme = had seen this movie.

target: Eu já tinha assistido a esse episódio.
english: I had already watched this episode.
tip: assistir meaning to watch needs the preposition a: assistido a esse episódio, not assistido esse.

target: Eu tenho pensado em mudar de carreira.
english: I've been thinking about changing careers.
tip: pensar pairs with em for think about: tenho pensado em mudar de carreira, where em marks the topic.

target: A gente tem se visto com frequência.
english: We've been seeing each other often.
tip: a gente means we but takes a singular verb: a gente tem se visto, never a gente temos.
